body:
Chief: M1'S PROBE DATA IS NOW IN docs/design/unforgeable-types.md, because it answers the question a slice author is most likely to get wrong.

THE TABLE: Mirror.ProductOf resolves for a bare-private constructor, a private[x] constructor, a bare-private constructor WITH A USER-WRITTEN COMPANION, and a private[x] constructor with one. All four. So WRITING YOUR OWN COMPANION WITH A SMART CONSTRUCTOR DOES NOT CLOSE THE DOOR - and that is exactly what an author will believe closes it, because it is the thing they just finished doing. If that belief had gone unchallenged across 44 slices we would have shipped 44 types that look guarded and are not.

The probe also pins the asymmetry precisely: bare private suppresses the GENERATED APPLY - BarePrivate.apply(1) does not compile - while leaving fromProduct intact. So apply and copy go, the Mirror stays. That is a strange shape and it is worth knowing rather than deducing.

I have also written the negative-assertion warning into the doc and into rule 4, with m1's two carriers cited as a case where it has ALREADY happened. An assert(!typeChecks(...)) returns false on any error and does not say which, so it can pass for an unrelated reason and keep passing through a mutation that should break it - which is precisely what m1 observed and could not explain. Positive control in the same file and scope, every time.

m1 has the migration backlog; collab has L1(b) and is doing the browser lifetime before the assertions, as ordered. Engineer silent 130 minutes; its lease expires 11:05:09Z and rule 5's threshold falls at 11:07. I will act on both together.
